sources.text:
Lofotodden National Park (Norwegian: Lofotodden nasjonalpark) is a national park located in Moskenes Municipality and Flakstad Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located not far from the Arctic Circle on the island of Moskenesøya in the Lofoten archipelago.
Lofotodden National Park was established on 22 June 2018. The national park covers an area of 99 square kilometres (38 sq mi), of which approximately 13 square kilometres (5.0 sq mi) is sea area. It was officially opened by Climate and Environment Minister Ola Elvestuen on 9 June 2019.


== Geography ==

The national park extends approximately 36 kilometres (22 mi) as the crow flies from the islets at the northern end of the island of Moskenesøya to the islands off the southwest coast. The protected area consists mainly of a mountain range with rugged peaks off the rugged west coast of the island, except for the southern part of Moskenes, which is part of the national park. The national park comprises the southern part of the 160-kilometre (99 mi) long mountain range, called Lofotenveggen (translated from Norwegian as "Lofoten Wall").
